mainTopic: Wording in a שכיב מרע's instructions, writing an unverified deathbed claim and the worry about a mistaken בית דין, and the father's produce rights
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about a שכיב מרע who orders two hundred זוז for someone he already owes. A wife given the money as her כתובה may choose either the money or her כתובה. A creditor told 'כראוי לו' gets the gift and his debt too, but if the words were 'בחובו', the gift pays the debt. רב נחמן, quoting רב הונא, explains that this follows רבי עקיבא, who reads extra words as adding something, as in the משנה about a seller who keeps a path to his בור and דות. Next comes a ברייתא about a שכיב מרע who says someone owes him a מנה: may עדים write this down without knowing it is true? רבי מאיר and חכמים argue, and a second version reverses their views, giving the worry about a בית דין that makes mistakes as the reason. רב דימי rules that we do not worry about such a בית דין. The גמרא challenges this from רבא's rule about חליצה and מיאון, and answers that a בית דין checks עדים carefully but does not double-check another בית דין. Finally, a new משנה teaches that a father who kept the produce rights may pick and give away produce, and picked produce goes to all the heirs. The גמרא infers that produce still attached to the ground does not.

steps.title: The wife chooses between the gift and her כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes the wife's case. When the money was given as her כתובה, she has the upper hand: she may take the two hundred זוז, or she may take her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She has the advantage. If she wants, she takes the two hundred זוז. If she wants, she takes her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: We join the ברייתא in the middle of a case. A dying man ordered two hundred זוז for his wife as her כתובה, and the ברייתא says she gets to choose which payment she prefers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the money was given 'as her כתובה', she does not collect both. She is not stuck with his amount either. She picks whichever is better for her: the two hundred זוז or her actual כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her hand is on top: she has the advantage and gets to choose
Her כתובה, the money a husband owes his wife from the marriage contract
She takes them (the two hundred זוז)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a case that started before this section. It is the case where he said the money is 'as her כתובה', not the case where she gets both.

phrases.english: Her hand is on top;
phrases.notes: An expression meaning she has the better position, so the choice is hers.

phrases.english: if she wants, she takes them,
if she wants, she takes her marriage contract payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the wife case of the ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the money was given as her כתובה, the wife chooses between the two hundred זוז and her full כתובה.

steps.title: The creditor case: 'as is appropriate for him' versus 'for his debt'
steps.stepSummary: A שכיב מרע orders two hundred זוז for his creditor. If he said 'as is appropriate for him', the creditor gets the money and also collects his debt. If he said 'for his debt', the money is the payment of the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: A dying man said: 'Give two hundred זוז to so-and-so, my creditor, as is appropriate for him.' The creditor takes the money and also collects his debt. But if he said 'for his debt', the creditor takes the money as payment of the debt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now teaches a matching case about a creditor. The exact words the dying man used decide whether the creditor gets an extra gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'For his debt' (בחובו) plainly means the money pays off the loan. 'As is appropriate for him' (כראוי לו) is treated as a separate gift, so the creditor collects the debt as well. The ruling depends only on the wording.

keyTerms.meaning: A person on his deathbed, whose spoken instructions about his property take effect
My creditor, someone I owe money to
As is appropriate for him
For his debt, as payment of what is owed

steps.whatToRemember: 'As is appropriate for him' means a gift plus the debt. 'For his debt' means the gift is the debt payment.

phrases.english: And a person on his deathbed who said:
"Give two hundred zuz to so-and-so,
my creditor, as is appropriate for him" –
he takes them, and he also takes his debt.
But if he said: "for his debt" –
he takes them as payment of his debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same ברייתא, moving from the wife case to a matching creditor case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'As is appropriate for him' gives the creditor the gift plus his debt. 'For his debt' makes the gift the payment of the debt.

steps.title: Why should 'as is appropriate for him' mean an extra gift?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Maybe 'as is appropriate for him' just meant 'what is owed to him for his debt', and not an extra gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because he said 'as is appropriate for him', the creditor takes the money and also his debt? Maybe he meant 'as is appropriate for him for his debt'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ruling for the creditor. It suggests the words could simply describe the debt being paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'as is appropriate for him' is unclear. It could easily mean 'what he deserves, namely his debt', which would make it the same as saying 'for his debt'. So why should the creditor collect twice?

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps: introduces another possible reading
He was saying

phrases.english: Because he said "as is appropriate for him" –
he takes them and also takes his debt?!
But perhaps he was saying "as is appropriate for him for his debt"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the creditor ruling of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that 'as is appropriate for him' gives the creditor both the gift and his debt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase can reasonably be read as describing the debt itself, so it should not create an extra gift.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who reads meaning into extra words
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רב הונא, answers that this ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא holds that extra wording is said for a reason, so it adds something new.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: הונא told me: Whose view is this? It is רבי עקיבא's view, since he reads meaning into extra words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by naming the author of the ברייתא: רבי עקיבא. It then gives the rule he follows about extra words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dying man could have just said 'give it to my creditor'. Adding 'as is appropriate for him' is extra wording. For רבי עקיבא, extra words show he meant to add something: a gift on top of the debt.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A way of naming the author of a teaching
Reads closely and draws meaning from
Extra, unnecessary wording

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that extra words in a person's instructions may add to what they give. That depends on following רבי עקיבא's approach.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Huna told me:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Akiva's,
who draws meaning from extra wording;
phrases.notes: 'As is appropriate for him' wasn't needed, so רבי עקיבא says it must add something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by naming the ברייתא's author.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Naming the author: the ברייתא follows a specific תנא's approach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'As is appropriate for him' might just describe the debt, so no extra gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי עקיבא, the extra phrase is meaningful and adds a gift on top of the debt.

steps.title: The source: selling a house without the pit and cistern
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where רבי עקיבא says a seller who kept the בור and דות must buy a path. He agrees that if the seller said 'חוץ מאלו', he does not need to buy a path.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone who sells a house has not sold the pit or the cistern, even if he wrote 'its depth and its height.' The seller must buy himself a path to reach them. This is רבי עקיבא's view. חכמים say he does not need to buy a path. רבי עקיבא agrees that if the seller said 'except for these', he does not need to buy a path.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing the משנה that proves רבי עקיבא thinks extra words add something. This sets up the comparison in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בור and דות are never included in a house sale anyway, so saying 'חוץ מאלו' is not needed. Still, רבי עקיבא says that once the seller said it, he also keeps a path to reach them. The unneeded words gave him something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A pit dug in the ground for holding water
A cistern, a water pit lined with stone
Its depth and its height, a broad phrase in a bill of sale
A path to walk through the buyer's property
Except for these

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'חוץ מאלו' is what keeps the בור and דות out of the sale. They are already left out without it. The extra words only give the seller the path.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: וְלֹא אֶת הַבּוֹר וְלֹא אֶת הַדּוּת,
phrases.english: As we learned: and not the pit and not the cistern,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה about someone who sells a house. He has not sold these along with it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁכָּתַב לוֹ עוּמְקָא וְרוּמָא.
phrases.english: even though he wrote for him 'depth and height.'
And he must buy himself a path,
phrases.notes: The seller has to buy the right to walk through the buyer's house to reach his pit and cistern.

phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say:
He does not need to buy himself a path.
And Rabbi Akiva agrees
when he said to him 'except for these' –
that he does not need to buy himself a path.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim in step 4 that רבי עקיבא holds extra words add something.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's rule that unneeded wording adds something new
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about selling a house without the בור and דות, where 'חוץ מאלו' gives the seller a path

steps.title: Applying the rule to 'as is appropriate for him'
steps.stepSummary: Just as unneeded words in the house sale added a path, unneeded words in the שכיב מרע's order ('כראוי לו') add a gift on top of the debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see that since he did not need to say it, and he said it anyway, it comes to add something. Here too, since he did not need to say it, and he said it anyway, it comes to add something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the lesson from the משנה and applies it to our ברייתא about the creditor. This finishes the answer from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, 'חוץ מאלו' was not needed, so it added a path. In our case, 'כראוי לו' was not needed, so it adds something too. That means the two hundred זוז are a gift on top of the debt.

keyTerms.meaning: So we see, apparently
Since he did not need to
To add something new
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, words that were not needed are not wasted. They add something. That is why the creditor who was given money 'כראוי לו' gets it as a gift and still collects his debt.

phrases.english: So we see: since he did not need to, and he said it –
it comes to add something;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּלָא צְרִיךְ, וְקָאָמַר –
phrases.english: here too, since he did not need to, and he said it –
it comes to add something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the principle out of the משנה in step 5 and applies it to the ברייתא from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That 'כראוי לו' gives the creditor a gift on top of his debt
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel to 'חוץ מאלו' in the house-sale משנה

steps.title: A dying man says someone owes him money: רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: a שכיב מרע says 'So-and-so owes me a מנה.' רבי מאיר says the עדים may write it even if they do not know it is true, so whoever collects must bring proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A שכיב מרע said, 'I have a מנה with so-and-so.' The witnesses may write it down even if they do not know it is true. So when it is collected, proof must be brought. This is רבי מאיר's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about a שכיב מרע who says someone owes him money. Here is רבי מאיר's side of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets the עדים write down the dying man's words even without knowing the debt is real. Because of that, the paper only records what he said and does not prove the debt. So whoever comes to collect still needs real proof.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of one hundred זוז
They know, meaning the witnesses know it is true
Collects a debt
Proof

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A dying person who said:
'I have a maneh with so-and-so' –
phrases.notes: Meaning: so-and-so owes me a hundred זוז.

phrases.english: the witnesses may write it,
even though they do not know.
Therefore, when he collects –
phrases.notes: 'He' is whoever comes to collect the debt later, such as the dying man's heirs.

phrases.english: he must bring proof,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא, still about the words of a שכיב מרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: עדים may write a dying man's claim without knowing it is true, so collecting requires outside proof.

steps.title: The view of חכמים: write only if you know
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say the עדים may write only if they know the debt is real. So the paper itself counts as proof, and no other proof is needed to collect.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: They do not write unless they know it is true. So when it is collected, no proof needs to be brought.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the other side of the argument in the ברייתא. חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about when the עדים may write.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, the עדים write only when they know the debt is real. So the written paper is trustworthy. That is why the one collecting does not need any other proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
Unless
Therefore

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the 'therefore' on both sides. The rule about proof follows from the rule about writing. If the עדים may write without knowing, the paper proves nothing. If they write only when they know, the paper is the proof.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכִּירִין,
phrases.english: They do not write unless they know,
therefore, when he collects –
he does not need to bring proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכִּירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: עדים write only when they know the debt is real, so the document itself is enough to collect.

steps.title: A second ברייתא where the opinions are switched
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רב הונא, brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר says the עדים may not write, and חכמים say they may write. Even רבי מאיר only says this out of fear that a בית דין will make a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: הונא told me that a ברייתא teaches the opposite. רבי מאיר says the עדים may not write the שכיב מרע's words, and חכמים say they may. Even רבי מאיר only said 'do not write' because a בית דין might make a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the ברייתא from steps 7-8, in which רבי מאיר and חכמים have switched positions. It also explains why רבי מאיר holds his view in this version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 7-8, רבי מאיר allowed writing and חכמים required knowing the debt was true. Here רבי מאיר forbids writing unless the עדים know. His only worry is that a mistaken בית דין will see the paper and let the heirs collect without any other proof.

keyTerms.meaning: They may not write it down
A בית דין that makes a mistake

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ברייתות. In the earlier one (steps 7-8), רבי מאיר says 'write.' In this one, רבי מאיר says 'do not write.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: Huna told me:

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין,
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir says: they may not write it,
phrases.notes: This is the reverse of the ברייתא in steps 7-8. Here רבי מאיר means they may not write unless they know the debt is true.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis say: they may write it.
And even Rabbi Meir did not say this
except because of a court that makes mistakes.
phrases.notes: The fear is that a court will see the paper and let the heirs collect without any other proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן, אָמַר לִי הוּנָא: תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a reversed version of the מחלוקת in steps 7-8 and gives the reason behind רבי מאיר's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רבי מאיר forbids writing an unverified claim, only out of concern for a בית דין that makes mistakes. חכמים allow it.

steps.title: The הלכה: no worry about a mistaken בית דין
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי of נהרדעא rules that we do not worry that a בית דין will make a mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי from נהרדעא said: the הלכה is that we do not worry about a בית דין that makes mistakes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a practical ruling: we do not worry that a בית דין will make this kind of mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי מאיר's only reason was the fear of a mistaken בית דין, removing that fear means the עדים may write the claim even if they do not know it is true. This ruling sets up the challenge in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The final practical law
We are not concerned
נהרדעא, a major Torah center in בבל

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle (אין חוששין לבית דין טועין) is what the גמרא now tests against רבא's ruling.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi of Nehardea said: the halacha is:
we are not concerned about a court that makes mistakes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the worry that step 9 gave as רבי מאיר's reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We do not worry that a בית דין will make a mistake.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge from רבא's rule about חליצה and מיאון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this is different from רבא. רבא says a בית דין may do חליצה or מיאון only if they recognize the people. Therefore a document of חליצה or מיאון may be written even without recognizing them.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from רבא? רבא said: we do not do חליצה unless the judges recognize the people, and we do not do מיאון unless they recognize the girl. Therefore one may write a גט חליצה or a גט מיאון even without recognizing them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a challenge by quoting רבא's rule. The real point of the question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא demands that the בית דין doing the חליצה or מיאון must know who the people are. Because of that strict rule, a later document can rely on it without checking again. The גמרא is about to suggest that רבא's strictness comes from worrying about a mistaken בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Performing חליצה (releasing a יבמה from יבום)
Performing מיאון (a girl married as a minor refuses the marriage)
They recognize, meaning they know who the people are
A document confirming that חליצה took place
A document confirming that מיאון took place

phrases.english: And how is this different from Rava?
For Rava said: we do not perform חליצה
unless the judges recognize the people,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְמָאֲנִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן מַכִּירִין.
phrases.english: and we do not perform מיאון unless they recognize her.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִיכָךְ כּוֹתְבִין גֵּט חֲלִיצָה וְגֵט מֵיאוּן,
phrases.english: Therefore one may write a document of חליצה or a document of מיאון,
even though they do not recognize the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against רב דימי's ruling by quoting רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's ruling that we do not worry about a בית דין that makes mistakes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא's strict rule seems to assume that a later בית דין might rely on a document without checking. That would be worrying about a mistaken בית דין.

steps.title: Isn't רבא worried about a mistaken בית דין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רבא's reason and suggests it must be a worry about a בית דין that makes mistakes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבא's reason? Isn't it because we worry about a בית דין that makes mistakes?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It argues that רבא's rule only makes sense if we worry about a mistaken בית דין, which goes against רב דימי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that רבא requires recognition because a later בית דין might trust a document blindly. If so, רבא does worry about a mistaken בית דין, which contradicts רב דימי's הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Is it not because...?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּחוֹשְׁשִׁין לְבֵית דִּין טוֹעִין?
phrases.english: Is it not because we are concerned about a court that makes mistakes?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּחוֹשְׁשִׁין לְבֵית דִּין טוֹעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge set up in step 11 by naming the reason behind רבא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבא's reason is a worry about a mistaken בית דין, then we do worry about it, which contradicts רב דימי.

steps.title: A בית דין checks עדים but not another בית דין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cases are different. A בית דין does not double-check another בית דין, but it does carefully check what עדים wrote.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. When a בית דין follows another בית דין, it does not check carefully. When a בית דין follows עדים, it does check carefully.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רבא's case and our case are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חליצה and מיאון, a later בית דין would trust the first בית דין without checking, so the first one must be careful to recognize the people. With the שכיב מרע's paper, only עדים wrote it, and a בית דין always checks עדים. So there is no fear that it will let someone collect with that paper alone, and רב דימי's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: They check carefully
After, or following

steps.whatToRemember: We do not worry about a mistaken בית דין when it is judging a paper from עדים, because a בית דין always checks עדים. We only worry when one בית דין relies on another, since courts trust each other without checking.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps רב דימי's ruling in place. The עדים may write the שכיב מרע's claim, because no בית דין will rely on their paper without checking.

phrases.english: No.

steps.title: The father may pick and give away produce, and picked produce goes to all heirs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a father who kept the produce rights may pick produce and feed it to whomever he likes. Produce already picked when he dies belongs to all the יורשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The father may pick produce and feed it to anyone he wants. Whatever he left already picked belongs to the heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives the rules for the produce in the case of a father who wrote his land to his son but kept the produce for himself during his lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The land itself already belongs to the son, but the father still controls the produce while he lives, so he may pick it and give it away freely. Once he dies, produce that was already picked counts as the father's own property. It therefore goes to all his יורשין, not only to the son who received the land.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Here it marks the start of a new משנה.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the split between picked produce, which counts as the father's, and still-growing produce, which goes with the land. The גמרא builds on that split in the next step.

steps.title: Only picked produce goes to all heirs, not produce still attached
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה closely: picked produce goes to all the heirs, but produce still attached to the ground does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Picked produce, yes, it goes to all the heirs. Attached produce, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a close reading from the wording of the משנה. This is a setup line that prepares the next move in the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה specifically said 'what he left picked,' so the גמרא infers that produce still attached to the ground at the father's death is treated differently. That produce stays with the land and belongs to the son who received it, not to all the heirs.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not for the heirs' does not mean nobody gets the attached produce. It goes with the land to the son who received the property.
